events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Shallow fog has developed across portions of the area due to a
combination of humid conditions and light winds. The fog could
become locally dense with visibilities down to a quarter mile,
especially in low-lying locations.

If traveling, be prepared for rapid changes in visibilities over
very short distances, make sure to slow down, and keep plenty of
stopping distance between yourself and other vehicles.

events.region: Modoc County; Klamath Basin; Northern and Eastern Klamath County and Western Lake County; Central and Eastern Lake County
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Temperatures between 38 and 33 degrees will result in frost
formation.

* WHERE...In California, Modoc County including the communities of
Alturas, Likely, Canby, and Lookout. In Oregon, parts of Klamath
County including the communities of Crescent, Chemult, Sprague
River, Beatty, Bly, Dairy, Bonanza, and Lorella. Additionally,
parts of Lake County including Fort Rock and across the Christmas
Valley, Silver Lake, and areas just east of Lakeview.

* WHEN...From 4 AM to 8 AM PDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Frost could harm sensitive outdoor vegetation. Sensitive
outdoor plants may be killed if left uncovered.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast; Central Brooks Range; Romanzof Mountains
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Snow. Total snow accumulations of 3 to 6 inches above
2000 feet and 1 to 3 inches below 2000 feet, with higher amounts
above pass level. Winds could gust as high as 30 mph over
Atigun Pass Tuesday night.

* WHERE...Central/Eastern Brooks Range and Eastern Arctic Coast.

* WHEN...Tuesday September 1st through Wednesday September 2nd.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Gusty winds could lead to
areas of blowing snow which could significantly reduce
visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of fronts working across the North
Slope will support moderate snow accumulations in this region.
Precipitation will remain predominantly snow in the Brooks
Range, with a rain/snow mix along the Eastern Arctic Coast on
Tuesday transitioning to all snow Tuesday night into Wednesday.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Through 800 am, areas of dense fog will reduce visibilities to a
quarter mile or less for portions of central and southern Minnesota,
and western Wisconsin.

If traveling this morning, be prepared for fog that could suddenly
reduce visibilities to 1/4 mile or less. Expect the fog to dissipate
by 800 am! Slow down and allow extra time to reach your destination.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Patchy dense fog will impact portions of the Charleston Metro area
and surrounding locations through daybreak. Visibilities as low as
1/4 mile can be expected at times. The nature of the fog is such that
visibilities will vary greatly over short distances with the risk for
locally dense fog being the greatest near bodies of water and other
low-lying areas such as marshes, swamps and large ditches. Motorists
should remain alert for these conditions this morning.
